design.md.new:
**Sub-decision: where money is quoted to the penny (revision 26, after verify-131; D229, in R2 since revision 26).** R2 said that every money figure is reported to the penny. verify-131 read that as reaching the memo's prose, which quotes a £0.60 payout as £1, as the previous release quoted every money figure. (i) To the penny everywhere, prose included: the prompt's metrics table and the offline model's prose would change, the committed example's prose would read differently from every memo the previous release wrote, and the guard would hold a hosted model to pence it has no reason to quote. (ii) To the penny where figures are recorded or tabulated, the evidence record, the appendix's figure table, the interactive table and every table built later; prose, and the prompt table and rule sentences it is drafted from, keep the whole pound, which the guard checks at the precision written. (iii) Prose to the penny for the money-in buckets only, so that the buckets quoted add up to M17 quoted: two conventions in one paragraph. *Chose (ii)*, the owner's answer (D229), which R2 says since revision 26. A credit memo quotes money in pounds, a person checking a figure reads the appendix or the drill-down, where the pence are, and the prose stays what the previous release wrote. What (ii) costs: the prose can quote buckets whose whole pounds do not add up to M17's whole pound, as rounded figures can; the appendix beside it shows the pence that do. *The pack's memo-ready section text* (R26): (a) the whole pound, as the memo's prose (design default, as R2 says since revision 26); (b) to the penny, as the appendix's figure table. (a) because the sections are the memo the underwriter copies, the guard checks them as it checks the memo, and the record beside them carries every figure to the penny with its lines. (b) suits a firm whose template quotes pence, at the cost of sections that read differently from the memo `cma run` drafts. The firm's template is open (E8), so revision 26 asks the owner; T24, which builds the sections, has not started.

**Sub-decision: M1 to M16 with a case profile (revision 26, after verify-130 and verify-131; D229, in R54, P2, P7 and R10 since revision 26).** M16 and M26 share one denominator, money in less lending drawdowns, returned direct debits and own-account transfers (Data changes). The previous release had no own-account category, so under v1 on its own no line is one, and M16 reads the previous release's lines. A case profile can name an own account, and under v1 a credit naming it is then an own-account transfer (src/cma/categorise.py:1302-1304 at 74ad8af), which leaves M16's denominator and evidence. (i) A case profile is new behaviour under any ruleset: M16 and M26 leave its own-account transfers out of their share, and M1 to M16 keep the previous release's lines only for a statement categorised by v1 on its own with no case profile. (ii) Under v1 a case profile is ignored, so v1 is the previous release exactly, with or without a case: the rollback flag would then drop every director and own account the underwriter entered, and a case rolled back to v1 would read differently from the same case under v2 for a reason no one sees. (iii) Under v1, M16 keeps own-account transfers in its denominator while M26 leaves them out: two denominators for two shares of one money in, which the design has kept as one since M26 was added. *Chose (i)*, the owner's answer (D229). What (i) costs: under v1 with a profile, M16's lines and value can differ from what the previous release would give the same statement; no committed or synthetic case carries a profile, so no committed figure moves. R5 and R6 apply under v1 as under v2, so a credit both kinds claim is ambiguous there too (C1).
